# A #[foreign] mark does not make a declaration foreign: the backend still
# emits it, body and all. So the lowering passes have to walk that body like
# any other.
#
# NoContext rewrites a context read into a hidden field on the component and
# threads it through every function that reads one. A function it skips keeps
# an ir.ContextRead, which no language emitter has a case for — the build panics
# rather than producing anything. Skipping the marked one is what an imported
# declaration deserves, because an import has no body here at all.

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=out app.sngl
grep 'func \(m Model\) label\(\) string' out/model.go
grep 'return \("theme=" \+ m.__ctx_theme\)' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"
import . "sngl:app"

context #theme("light")

#[foreign("js:./api", "label")]
func label() string {
    return "theme=" + theme
}

component Toolbar {
    text(value=label())
}

window #home(title="Home", href="/") {
    theme("dark") {
        Toolbar()
    }
}
